text: True or False: For Plato in the Timaeus, time is ontologically inferior to eternity - a created, moving image that depends upon, and only imperfectly approximates, an unchanging eternal model.
explanation: This is true. In the Timaeus the eternal model (the realm of Being) is the original, while time belongs to the realm of Becoming; the temporal cosmos is a copy that depends on the eternal for its existence and never fully attains it. Plato draws ontological, epistemic, and evaluative asymmetries that all rank eternity above time.
